problems.memo_sentence: "The study uses a Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC) as a hybrid quantum–classical model, in which classical feature vectors are amplitude-encoded into an n-qubit system and processed by a parameterized quantum circuit."
problems.source_evidence: "State preparation refers to encoding classical input data into the quantum system... In this process, amplitude encoding is used." and "The model circuit is the part that processes the data transferred to the quantum system and performs classification."
problems.explanation: The paper describes amplitude encoding as part of state preparation, but it does not explicitly say the whole VQC is defined by amplitude-encoding feature vectors into an n-qubit system in the broad way the memo states. The memo slightly over-specifies the encoding mechanism as if it were the central model definition.

problems.memo_sentence: "The authors caution that their findings are obtained entirely on quantum simulators, so the reported results, while promising, may not fully reflect performance in real deployment scenarios. They explicitly note that the simulators are constrained by limited qubit availability and gate depth, which restricts scalability and may differ from the behavior on actual noisy quantum hardware."
problems.source_evidence: "However, one important limitation of the current work is the reliance on quantum simulators, which do not fully capture the noise, decoherence, and execution constraints present in real quantum hardware." and "In addition, the simulators used in this study were constrained by limited qubit availability and gate depth, which restrict the scalability of the model."
problems.explanation: This limitation is correctly mentioned, but the memo omits another explicit limitation: the simulators do not capture noise, decoherence, and execution constraints of real hardware. That is a substantive part of the paper’s cautionary framing.

problems.memo_sentence: "For future work, the authors recommend validating the proposed quantum models on real quantum hardware and scaling to larger datasets, to assess how the approach behaves beyond simulator constraints and closer to operational fraud-detection settings."
problems.source_evidence: "In future studies, it is recommended to test quantum models on real hardware with larger data sets." and "Moreover, future investigations should incorporate aspects such as model interpretability, fairness, and adversarial robustness, particularly important in financial fraud contexts where decisions must be transparent, ethical, and secure."
problems.explanation: The memo captures the real-hardware/larger-dataset recommendation but misses additional future-work directions explicitly stated in the conclusion: interpretability, fairness, and adversarial robustness. These are not minor details; they are concrete future research items.

problems.memo_sentence: "The paper primarily compares different feature selection strategies feeding a quantum VQC (traditional K-Best versus meta-heuristics PSO, ACO, ASO) rather than directly benchmarking against end-to-end classical classifiers... but no explicit runtime or accuracy comparison to purely classical models is reported."
problems.source_evidence: The results section includes a comparison table of prior classical and hybrid methods: "Table 1 An overview of the literature" with classical models such as XGBoost, RF, CNN, LSTM/GRU/MLP, SVM/KNN/RF, etc., and their reported performances, alongside "Our system" with "Meta-heuristic feature selection-VQC".
problems.explanation: The memo is broadly right that the paper’s main experiments compare feature-selection strategies within VQC, but it underplays that the paper also situates its method against a literature table of classical and hybrid approaches. This is a mild section-bias issue because the memo emphasizes the abstract-level framing more than the paper’s comparative context.
